title: Percentile-sliced latency emitter and per-model/region regression alerts
creator: Marcus Nguyen
description: Add a lightweight percentile-slice emitter that produces p50/p90/p95/p99 latency metrics grouped by route, model variant, region, and request_size_bucket. Integrate these metrics into Grafana dashboards and a regression detector that raises alerts when a slice deviates from baseline traffic behavior. The goal is to enable fast triage for customer-facing latency regressions without exploding metrics cardinality.
acceptance_criteria: Emitter produces per-minute p50/p90/p95/p99 for combinations: route x model x region x size_bucket for top 300 active slices
Grafana dashboard 'Perf Slices — route/model/region' populated with referenced metrics and useful drilldowns
Regression detector runs daily baseline calculation and raises alerts (PagerDuty/Slack) when p95 increases > 30% and absolute p95 crosses 200ms for a slice
Load harness (tokens/sec) can replay recorded production traces against the emitter and show matching percentile deltas within 10%
Implementation respects sampling budget: max 5% extra telemetry cost under normal traffic and falls back to sampling when cardinality thresholds are reached
Docs: Confluence runbook for triage and a short SDK doc for teams to add custom size_buckets
technical_notes: Design: compute percentiles at the edge collector using a streaming t-digest and emit per-minute rollups to metrics pipeline rather than raw histograms to control cardinality
Slice selection: maintain an LRU of top-N active slices (by request count) with periodic re-evaluation; fall back to coarse 'all' slice for low-volume tails
Baselining: use 28-day rolling median and IQR to detect anomalies; combine relative threshold (pct increase) and absolute threshold to reduce noise
Storage: metrics emitted as prometheus-style timeseries with labels: route, model, region, size_bucket, quantile. Downstream will store in ClickHouse/Timescale depending on config
Alerting: regression detector runs as a daily job in 'observability' namespace; high-severity triggers PagerDuty, medium => Slack #perf-alerts
Cost control: implement dynamic sampling gate that reduces slice emission frequency during sustained high-cardinality events (e.g., deployments)
Backward compatibility: emitter respects existing metrics schema and can be toggled per-cluster via feature flag 'percentile_slice_emitter'
Security: no user PII should be included; slice keys only derived from route identifier and model id

updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting — agreed on t-digest at edge to reduce downstream pressure. Observability prefers ClickHouse for long-term retention.
2026-02-28: Prototyped t-digest module; initial microbench shows +1.8% CPU on collector under p95 heavy traffic. We will gate rollout to non-prod first.
2026-03-03: Design review completed. Decision: top-300 active slices to cap cardinality. A follow-up task added to make top-N configurable per-region.
2026-03-07: Metrics pipeline PR opened (423). Early reviewer feedback: add metric label 'size_bucket' format and avoid freeform strings. Adjusted to predefined buckets [small, medium, large, xlarge].
2026-03-10: Regression detector initial implementation done; running in dry-run mode for 48h. Observed 6 false positives from Canary traffic — tuning thresholds planned.
2026-03-10: Assignee note: moving acceptance criterion on alerts to require both relative and absolute thresholds to limit noise. Next: dashboard finalization and canary rollout to staging clusters.
dashboards: tokens-per-sec-vs-p95 (Grafana): overlay tokens/sec load test traces with percentile bands
slice-health-summary (Grafana): top-300 slices by error rate and latency regression status
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: metric cardinality growth during large-scale experiments could spike observability costs. Mitigation: enforce top-N selection, dynamic sampling, and a hard cap with graceful degradation to coarse slices.
Risk: false positives from transient deployment noise. Mitigation: require sustained deviation over configurable window (default 15m) and double-threshold rule (relative + absolute).
Risk: collector CPU regression. Mitigation: CPU budget testing in staging and feature-flagged gradual rollout; revert plan documented in runbook.
